items.text: Russian missiles struck Kyiv early on 7 Nov, injuring at least five, closing a Dnipro bridge and damaging energy facilities in the Kyiv and Zhytomyr regions; Mayor [[p:Vitali Klitschko]] called the capital's power situation "extremely difficult". The death toll from the 2 Nov guided-bomb strike on Komyshuvakha rose to 55. The attacks come days before the US–Russia–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 Nov.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes

items.text: US forces carried out a new "limited" strike on an Iranian air-defence system on Qeshm Island on 6 Nov; Iranian state media reported two explosions near Suza. [[p:Donald Trump]] called it "minor" and said Washington is talking to Tehran. Iran says it will not start nuclear talks until the blockade ends, sanctions are lifted and frozen assets released.

Border fighting continued. Pakistani officials in South Waziristan say [[p:Taliban]] forces fired on their posts near Angoor Adda on 1 Nov and Pakistan struck several Taliban posts and mortar positions in return, reporting no Pakistani casualties. Taliban police in Paktika say Pakistani fire on homes in Shkin district the same day killed one civilian and wounded two. There were also clashes at Torkham. Neither side's account is independently confirmed.
items.notes: Each side attributes the start of fire to the other.

items.text: More than 20 rights groups called for the release of lawyer Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha, calling the case a "misuse of the criminal justice system". An antiterrorism court sentenced each on 29 Oct to 10 years in a "security breach" case over removed barriers, plus shorter terms for obstructing and assaulting officials.
items.notes: Sentencing was 29 Oct, just before the window; included because this is the first brief for the segment.

items.text: Suspected militants killed two policemen guarding a polio vaccination team in Mohmand, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; police suspect the [[p:Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan]].
France's interior minister told parliament that Paris has opened technical talks with the Taliban on returning Afghans without legal residence. No Taliban response was reported.
The Taliban's economic deputy PM's office says it held a meeting to coordinate economic cooperation with Russia and review bilateral agreements.

Thousands joined a [[p:Indian National Congress]]-led rally in New Delhi demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over the [[e:Special Intensive Revision]] of voter rolls, which removed more than 130 million names. The opposition says Muslims and other minorities were disproportionately hit; the [[p:Election Commission of India|Election Commission]] denies bias and says wrongly removed voters can re-register.
items.notes: Near-daily protests since late September; the Tribune reports the opposition is weighing impeachment of the CEC.

items.text: The Union Cabinet approved ₹2,814 crore in capital subsidies for four lithium and nickel processing plants, ₹14,500 crore in viability-gap funding for 92 GWh of grid storage, and an extension of fast-track courts for rape and child-abuse cases to 2031.

The UN General Assembly, without objection, extended Bangladesh's transition out of least-developed-country status by three years, to 24 Nov 2029. The EU backed it as an "exceptional time-bound" step tied to a 2026–29 reform roadmap it and the UN will monitor.
items.notes: Vote date inferred as Thursday 29 Oct; before window, first segment brief.

items.text: PM [[p:Tarique Rahman]] returned from a four-day Japan visit with two yen loans worth ¥46.6bn (about $296m), a ¥2.1bn grant for a coast-guard patrol vessel and 17 private-sector MoUs. A proposed ¥1tn private investment package was discussed but not signed.
On National Revolution and Solidarity Day, Tarique Rahman urged unity and closed with the slogan "Not Delhi, not Pindi… Bangladesh first."

An emergency cabinet meeting removed police chief Dan Bahadur Karki and appointed Manoj Kumar KC, days after police entered newsrooms and detained journalists over reports that Karki would be sacked. Ruling [[p:Rastriya Swatantra Party]] chair [[p:Rabi Lamichhane]] publicly questioned due process, exposing friction with PM [[p:Balen Shah]]'s government.
items.notes: Kathmandu Post cites officials on the reasons (the Inam Sapkota probe and stalled arrest orders); the government says the move was not punitive.

items.text: The [[p:European Commission]]'s 2026 enlargement report called Georgia "an EU candidate in name only", citing three years of backsliding on the judiciary and fundamental rights, the abolished anti-corruption bureau, and the bid to ban five opposition parties. Georgia's foreign ministry said the report reinforced "anti-Georgian narratives".
items.notes: Foreign ministry reaction from a Civil Georgia headline (page not readable).

items.text: Justice Minister Srbuhi Galyan said the draft of Armenia's new constitution should be published in November under her ministry. Publication would not automatically start a referendum campaign. A new constitution is Azerbaijan's main precondition for signing the peace treaty.
items.outlet: Massis Post; Public Radio of Armenia

items.text: President [[p:Ilham Aliyev]] skipped the [[p:Organization of Turkic States]] summit in Ankara, sending his foreign minister, amid a rift with Turkey over Baku's school hijab ban and its ties with Israel. Baku barred more than 30 Turkish critics from entry; [[p:Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] told the summit there was "no room for division".
items.notes: One day before the window; included as first segment brief.

items.text: Energy Minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov said he formally asked Moscow to reopen Kazakh oil transit to Germany via the [[p:Druzhba pipeline]], halted by Russia since 1 May. A drone attack on Russian infrastructure stopped the Atyrau–Samara pipeline on 2 Nov; flows resumed the next day.
A senior AKP official said Russia does not qualify for observer status in the Organization of Turkic States, pushing back on [[p:Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]]'s proposal at the 30 Oct Ankara summit.
Astana co-hosted an Aqaba Process counter-terrorism meeting with Jordan; [[p:Shavkat Mirziyoyev]] offered to host a regional UN counter-terrorism office in Uzbekistan.
